history.note: harness until the mode-cutoff restart (borg-zoo#54). The runner and observer are unchanged at the new pin; the bump keeps the harness commit at the specimens' tree after the 0100/0101/0101a fixes. A proposed runner change that would have recorded the applied configuration text (better-borg-c PR 435) was closed as mis-filed and is not needed: configuration_sha256 already identifies what a run applied.
live watchdog read could abort a run on a split UTF-8 character (better-borg-c#220); fixed by 56ccf741. The observer is unchanged between the two pins.

harness.note: The better-borg-c runner and observer at this commit build and run every specimen. A specimen is the game and Borg source at its own ref; the observer instrumentation comes from the harness commit. It applies to specimens of kind "better-borg-c" (the default). Specimens of kind "borg-rs" are built and run by borg-rs's own harness at the specimen's ref (harness/build.sh and the borgh frontend). This pin is also a specimen ref (4.2.6-bbc-9ca98661): the harness bumped with the mode-cutoff restart so runner and specimens move together (borg-zoo#54).

experiment.owner_authorization: 2026-11-22: borg-reborn-rs owner ("file the zoo request for part 2 in the breeder worlds"), filed as borg-zoo#659; zoo owner, 2026-11-22: "yes do all that" (the classes-18 pilot only; small + medium after the gate and the owner).
experiment.prespecified:
Fixed 2026-11-22, before any result of this build was read (borg-zoo#659; borg-reborn-rs #881, PR #953). Six profiles on one build, classes-18,
18 starts each (108 cells), 100,000 exact engine turns, evidence retained: ctl, d1 and d2 in breeders-x4 and in breeders-x8 (a world's arms are
compared only within that world). caution_retreat_dead_end_distance stays 6. Gate: no config_error; one binary; every cell records its world
with the same borg_world_data_sha256 in every arm of that world; each arm's value in params-core.json; every cell ends in death, turn_cap or
borg_stopped with frozen-turn bursts classified; death bundles reproduce in the same world; the arms must play differently: the rule writes no
note, so if d1 or d2 plays identically to ctl in all 18 pilot games of a world, stop and report before the larger tiers. Primary: deaths by
100,000 turns; mean CL and depth may each fall by no more than 0.25 against ctl in the same world. Report per world, arm and class: deaths and
causes and breeder deaths (the killer has MULTIPLY); paired rescued and newly killed against ctl (exact McNemar) and identical plays; final and
maximum CL, deepest level; unfinished games with denominators; a RULES 18 bin. Diagnostics: per game the "# Retreating to" and "# Backing up to"
notes against ctl, breeder exits, flee and escape notes, "# Breeders cannot be stopped" and "No rest: ... breeders known", breeders created and
killed. A breeder world is a stress test; a confirmation needs an unopened seed block. Directional (RULES 14).
experiment.question: In the breeders-x4 and breeders-x8 worlds on borg-reborn-rs b157f9dd (PR #953), does refusing a dead end (mode 1) or a grid farther from the way out than the Borg's own (mode 2) in the strategic retreat and the back-up save the games lost inside a one-exit lattice room of worm masses? Each world has its own control.
